idea: A news page built as a broadsheet front page above a dense sortable table of every story, with imagery supplying all colour.
An agency homepage reduced to a typeset index on one offset grid, using two typefaces and a single red.
A developer's huge navy wordmark sits inside the house photograph, then slides across the page as a poster-like opening move.
One continuous colour atmosphere rises as a blurred glow from the page floor and re-tints itself for each project shown.
The pipeline is explained by literally running interface cards through a scanner, so the diagram is the demonstration itself.
One isometric hairline machine dismantles itself as you scroll, making an abstract data engine physically understandable part by part.
A team index whose only design is live library statistics drawn as sparklines beside each member's name.
An agency homepage reduced to one prompt and one endless rail of work, with no navigation and no scrolling.
Checkout is told as a very long scroll film where a phone changes state at each stop along a floating island.
A single stair-step pixel shape drives the logo, hero glyph, panel corners and patterned patches across the whole page.
One interactive WebGL creature is the entire interface, and the list of work orbits around it.
The site is five keyboard-driven slides, each showing a live wireframe data sketch on blank paper, working like an instrument.
A brand studio drops all selling and offers only a long silent scroll of four-up image blocks.
An architecture studio strips every interface convention and shows its whole body of work as one long single-file column of buildings.
An entire CV is compressed into one screen of pastel accordion blocks that read like a personal card.
Enterprise software is sold through a sleeping baby photograph instead of a dashboard, with the product appearing only as a quiet caption.
A robotics company is presented as a quiet fashion campaign, with soft robots on grey and full-screen scenes carrying one line each.
A camera brand's home page is an edge-to-edge contact sheet of photographers shooting with the product, captioned in condensed type.
A slit-cut square logo serves as the hero, the scroll object and the footer, so one shape is the whole page.
An artist's site is a single framed photograph surrounded by oversized text, with the name bending across the picture as you scroll.
A one-screen holding page: one 3D logomark, one serif sentence and two links, with the background slowly drifting between warm and cool.
One huge wordmark runs across the bottom over a rapidly cross-fading slideshow of artist photographs.
An intro collage resolves into a horizontal film strip of portrait tiles with a running counter.
Founders' portraits are scattered across a cream page as the hero, and the page dissolves into a sky gradient as you scroll.
A layered illustrated sunset scene with characters is the entire interface, working like a storybook rather than a website.
A white void holds a single vertical column of object photographs to scroll through, flanked by tiny index labels.
Each full-screen paper-craft stop-motion colour world carries exactly one fact about the company, told as a story.
A sentence bends along a scrolling curve while a red car and an illustrated balloon scene replace the usual sections.
A giant serif year-count numeral rolls like an odometer over a painterly dark field as a tribute.
A scroll-driven ring shows live demos of each library feature in a central circle that morphs through 3D scenes.
A single white screen shows a floating cluster of glossy project spheres around a core, with only one contact button.
A residence presentation runs from a warm intro into a blue wireframe 3D house that you explore by scrolling.
A portfolio reduced to one centred image at a time with two lines of caption, letting the work carry everything.
A portfolio built as an instrument: a radial clock dial on the left controls a single project image deck on the right.
A restaurant homepage is one full-bleed dusk photograph of the building with only a bottom navigation strip.
A 3D gallery of illustrated player cards orbits a trophy, fans into a carousel and scrubs along a radial index.
Sign-up is the hero, wrapped by a wire diagram of people and agents handing off work, so the idea becomes the structure.
A soda brand runs as a surreal scrapbook where vintage cut-outs and ink drawings float on pure white around plain type.
A personal site reduced to one narrow column of prose and a three-column index, where typography alone carries hierarchy.
A restaurant homepage is a full-viewport blurred dreamscape with a hand-painted logo and rotating bilingual captions.
An artist's painting archive is reduced to a dense edge-to-edge grid of colourful works with only tiny text.
A black single screen of four outlined sticker mascots, one per product family, with a centred logo and a row of links.
A venture firm shows nearly nothing: one phrase, then a horizontal strip of portfolio tiles on pure black.
A production company portfolio is a scattered poster wall with an enormous condensed title that swaps for each project.
Scroll turns a single plate into breakfast, then dinner and beyond, pacing a beach club's day with full-bleed sea photography.
A looping video of venetian blinds is the entire page, with sentences and thumbnail slivers hidden in the slats.
A pan-and-zoom constellation of names, concerts and photographs orbits a centred wordmark on near-black.
A near-white spatial canvas of project panes that you pan sideways, with a toggle between info and work.
An architecture portfolio spread where a tall photograph slides across a blank white page with name and place at the margins.
Giant product names wipe through vertical blade-like slats as each knife and its colour swap, in a tactile grey world.
Navigation is a floating orbit of tilted photo cards that drift past a ghosted list of categories.
A publisher's shop uses one electric ink colour on cream as the whole interface, so book covers supply every other colour.
A scroll of giant possessive headlines, each with a tiny hand-drawn diagram and a short caption, reads like an index of interviews.
An architecture studio is expressed through flat colour blocks and a letter-shaped photo cut-out carrying large statements.
A release log becomes a dated gallery where every small change gets its own monochrome poster on a black timeline.
The homepage is the product itself: a single composer on a quiet canvas with a sidebar as the only navigation.
A craft studio's closing letter is set as one enormous thank-you between warm documentary photographs.
The homepage is simply a terminal window playing an ASCII animation of the product's mascot.
The landing page behaves like a code repository, with a fixed title panel beside a scrolling readme.
The homepage skips marketing and shows the live feed itself, led by a single pitch card.
The homepage is replaced by a scrolling manifesto whose words darken one by one, edged by pixel texture.
A venture firm is staged as an unmapped chart, with hairline rails, vanishing-point grids and stippled coastlines carrying one idea.
The product page is the real analytics dashboard itself, public and data dense, closed by a single pitch.
A venture firm's home is one screen with a cinematic film reel and a gold slogan, and no scrolling.
A biscuit maker turns the scalloped edge of its product into the shape language of the entire site.
An agency homepage is reduced to one sentence, a client list and a looping liquid object, persuaded by its load sequence.
A durable-execution pitch proves itself with a runnable failure demo instead of claims, set on black with square controls.
A product launch staged as a darkroom joke where a spotlit device casts an absurdly long shadow that becomes the page.
A one-colour competition microsite builds its headline, layout and exit out of red, treating winning artworks as raw material.
A modular shelf brand borrows its product's logic: a pegboard grid of swappable shapes with one surprise at the end.
A storybook expedition told as one long scroll along a hand-drawn trail through engravings, slides and field notes.
A scroll-flown point-cloud city serves as the architect's portfolio index, with plain cream chrome supplying the facts.
One continuous hand-drawn line threads through every section of the page in place of stock visuals.
A museum's site is a chronological column of works with a bitmap wordmark and one physical blue ball reacting to scroll.
A studio page is a live instrument where wind data from outside bends the typography itself.
A fashion homepage removes headlines, buttons and metadata, letting campaign images, two type sizes and a hard 50/50 split carry the store.
An experimental school's index page is just four volumes and four dates with no interface chrome.
A photographer's portfolio is a moving gallery wall where scattered prints collapse into a deck, then one pinned image at a time.
A watch is sold as a scroll-driven teardown: one render stays pinned while it is exploded and inspected chapter by chapter.
A themed image archive is organised around a live clock drawn at the scale of the whole page.
A gateway page asks a single question, which city, with two dimmed interior photographs and nothing else.
An entry page that is one generative line drawing with two links.
An artist's site is staged as a three-panel book opened by a hand-written monogram and turned by deliberate scrolling.
A watch launch withholds the site behind a full-screen exploded-view film with a progress counter.
A professional group's homepage is one screen of four colour-coded columns, each acting as a small identity for one company.
A theatre photography archive is one sliding stack of prints on a white wall, with years pinned to the corners.
A studio site is one steel-blue wordmark in a white void, with a new polished object appearing on every scroll.
A monogram stays pinned to the viewport corners while projects drift through a bone-coloured frame like rooms seen through a doorway.
The slash in a museum's logo becomes the page's single geometric idea, cutting the hero, dividers and info strip at one angle.
A glass brand tells its whole story as one display-size paragraph on charcoal, ending on outlined links over macro video.
A full-screen particle globe where each light is a language, with a calm search-first interface floating above it.
A studio replaces headlines with a shuffled deck of work, where each project recolours the small interface around it.
A studio home is one sideways rail of tall work images, with intro and news slotted in as just another column.
A consultancy's whole site is one fixed six-cell poster mixing flat colour, a serif logotype and two photographs.
A tile museum builds its whole interface from its subject, using roof-tile friezes, fired clay textures and a paper ground.
A portfolio declines to be one: a single unscrolling sheet of small bold text set like a printed credits page.
A studio reel is one long pinned stack where two matched trays stay fixed while client images and loops pass between them.
A whiteboard product page that behaves like a whiteboard, with sticker collage, sticky notes and live cursors over stark type.
